Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates dense, curvilinear calcifications outlining the anterior and inferior aspects of the cardiac silhouette, specifically following the contour of the right ventricle and atrioventricular grooves. This pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which can present with heart murmurs and hemodynamic compromise.
